                    ### Question
                    A 25-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after he was involved in a motorcycle collision. He was not wearing a helmet. Physical examination shows left periorbital ecchymosis. A CT scan of the head shows a fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure. Physical examination of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Decreased sense of smell
opb. Numbness of the left cheek
opc. Preserved left lateral gaze
opd. Absent left corneal reflex
ope. Complete loss of vision of the left eye

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The fracture of the greater wing of the left sphenoid bone with compression of the left superior orbital fissure can lead to damage of cranial nerves III, IV, VI, and V1. This results in several potential findings. The absent left corneal reflex (option d) is likely due to sensory loss from the involvement of the trigeminal nerve (V1), which is responsible for the corneal reflex. The involvement of the oculomotor nerve (CN III) can cause ptosis and pupillary abnormalities, but does not directly correlate with the corneal reflex. The abducens nerve (CN VI) involvement would lead to impaired lateral gaze, contradicting option c. Numbness of the left cheek (option b) can occur due to maxillary nerve (V2) involvement. Complete loss of vision (option e) is less likely unless the optic nerve (CN II) is directly affected, which is not typically the case with this type of fracture. Therefore, the most likely physical examination finding is absent left corneal reflex due to V1 involvement.
